name: Ace of Cups
symbols: A hand from a cloud holds a chalice — the gift arrives from beyond the self.
A dove descends into the cup — peace, spirit, the messenger.
Water overflows in five streams — emotion that is being given rather than hoarded.
A pond of lotus flowers — purity, the surface where the deepest things rise.

reading.upright: The Ace of Cups is the beginning of feeling: new love, intuitive opening, the cup that overflows. It is receptivity, not pursuit.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the cup is closed or empty: emotion repressed, love refused, the intuition that has been walled off.

elementalRegister.value: Water (Cups; the chalice, the dove, the overflowing water)
elementalRegister.note: The Ace of Cups is the root of the water suit: the beginning of feeling, the cup that overflows with emotion and intuition.

numericalDegree.note: The Ace is the root of the suit, the seed of the element. It is the degree of pure potential, before the number has begun to differentiate.

courtFunction.note: The Ace is not a court card; it is the elemental root of the suit.

figureType.value: A hand from a cloud, holding a chalice, with a dove descending
figureType.note: The hand is the only figure. It comes from the cloud, marking the gift as from beyond the self. The dove is the messenger of peace.

posture.value: The hand holds the chalice upright
posture.note: The upright posture of the chalice is the posture of reception: the cup is held open, ready to receive.

gesture.value: Holding the chalice, the dove descending into it
gesture.note: The gesture is one of offering and reception. The hand offers the cup; the dove descends into it.

gaze.note: There is no gaze. The Ace is not a personality; it is a force.

movementDirection.value: Static (the cup is held, the water overflows)
movementDirection.note: There is no directional movement. The Ace is the point of opening, not the journey.

centralObject.note: The chalice is the vessel of feeling; the dove is the messenger of peace. Both are the symbols of the card's opening.

heldObject.note: The chalice is held by the hand from the cloud. It is the gift of the element.

creature.note: The dove is the creature of peace and the messenger of the spirit. It descends into the cup, marking the feeling as blessed.

tool.note: The tool is the chalice, the instrument of the water suit.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The Ace's law is the feeling itself, not a written instruction.

landscape.note: The landscape is the pond, the surface of the water where the deepest things rise. The lotus is the flower of purity.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The Ace is in the open, at the source of the water.

threshold.note: The cloud is the threshold between the unseen and the seen. The hand emerges from it, bringing the feeling into the world.

celestialBody.note: The clouds are the celestial source of the gift. The feeling comes from above, not from the earth.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The Ace is the clear moment of opening.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the hand from the side, the pond below)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The Ace is a point of departure, not a balance.

repetitionCount.note: The five streams are the overflow of feeling, the abundance of the cup.

verticalAxis.value: The hand from above, the pond below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the celestial (the cloud) to the earthly (the pond). The cup is the point of connection.

horizontalAxis.value: The cup held to the side, the dove descending
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the offering: the cup is held out, the dove descends.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The Ace is upright and open.

clothing.note: There is no clothing. The Ace is the bare element, without the mediation of culture.

nudity.note: There is no body. The Ace is the element itself, not a person.

crown.note: There is no crown. The Ace is the root of the suit, not a figure of authority.

wound.note: There is no wound. The Ace is pure potential, not yet marked by experience.

binding.note: There are no chains. The feeling is free.

water.value: The overflowing water and the pond
water.note: Water is the element of the card. It is the feeling that overflows and the pool from which the lotus rises.

fire.note: There is no fire. The Ace of Cups is the root of water.

vegetation.note: The lotus is the flower of purity, rising from the water. It marks the feeling as sacred.

stone.note: There is no stone. The Ace is the element of water, not of earth.

polarity.note: The Ace of Cups' remedy-pair is the Ace of Wands: water and fire, feeling and will. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Ace of Cups' pure feeling is the Ace of Wands' spark: sometimes the feeling needs to be corrected by the will to act.

prescribedAct.value: Let one feeling arrive today without naming it or explaining it, and let it overflow.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of reception. The Ace of Cups' lesson is that feeling is a gift that must be received, not seized.

detailedReading: The Ace of Cups is the root of the water suit: the beginning of feeling, the cup that overflows. Its elemental register is water, and its numerical degree is the Ace, the seed of the element. The figure is a hand from a cloud, holding a chalice, with a dove descending into it. The landscape is the pond of lotus flowers, the surface of the water where the deepest things rise. There is no creature other than the dove, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the Ace is the pure element, free and open. The asymmetry of the composition marks it as a point of departure. The prescribed act follows from this: let one feeling arrive today without naming it or explaining it, and let it overflow. The remedy is will — the Ace of Wands — because the feeling needs to be corrected by the capacity to act.

name: Two of Cups
symbols: Two figures face each other, cups raised — exchange, mutual regard, a meeting of equals.
A caduceus hovers between them — harmony, healing, the alignment of two wills.
A winged lion's head — passion, sanctified by the exchange.
Both cups held at the same height — the exchange is balanced.

reading.upright: The Two of Cups is the meeting of equals: partnership, mutual attraction, the felt connection between two people or two parts of the self.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the balance fails: a relationship that has become one-sided, or a connection that no longer meets.

elementalRegister.value: Water (Cups; the exchanged cups, the caduceus)
elementalRegister.note: The Two of Cups is the water element in its phase of union. The exchanged cups mark it as the card of mutual regard and partnership.

numericalDegree.note: Two is the number of polarity and pairing. The card is the moment at which the single feeling of the Ace meets another and becomes a partnership.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Two is the first differentiation of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: Two standing human figures, facing each other, each holding a cup
figureType.note: The figures are human and paired. Their equal stances mark the card as one of meeting, not of dominance.

posture.value: Standing upright, facing each other, cups raised
posture.note: The posture is one of exchange: the figures are open to each other, the cups held at the same height.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of offering and receiving. The cups are lifted as gifts, not as weapons.

gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of mutual regard. The figures are looking at each other, not away.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the pause of the meeting.

centralObject.value: The two cups and the caduceus
centralObject.note: The cups are the offerings; the caduceus is the harmony between them. Together they mark the card as one of union.

heldObject.note: The cups are held, one in each figure's hand. The holding is the holding of the offering.

creature.value: A winged lion's head above the caduceus
creature.note: The winged lion is the creature of passion, sanctified by the exchange. It marks the card as one of blessed union.

tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the exchange: the cups that are raised.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The union is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: An open ground with a house behind
landscape.note: The landscape is the open ground and the house: the meeting is in the world, with the home as its horizon.

architecture.note: The house is the architecture of the home. It is distant, marking the card as the meeting that is not yet the household.

threshold.note: There is no threshold. The card is the meeting, not the crossing.

celestialBody.note: There is no celestial body. The union is ordinary, not cosmic.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The card is the calm day of the meeting.

symmetry.value: Balanced (the two figures face to face)
symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the meeting, not the imbalance of the dominance.

repetitionCount.note: The number two is the number of the pairing. The two cups mark the card as one of mutual exchange.

verticalAxis.value: The figures above the ground, the cups at the same height
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis is the axis of the exchange: the cups are at the same height, marking the card as one of equals.

horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the meeting: the figures are facing each other across the ground.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figures are upright and open.

clothing.note: The varied robes mark the figures as distinct persons, not a uniform. The card is a meeting of two distinct selves.

nudity.note: The figures are clothed. Their meeting is mediated by their social positions.

crown.note: There is no crown, but the wreaths are the mark of the celebration. The meeting is a crowning of the two.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of union, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figures are free to meet or to part.

water.value: Absent (the cups are the only water)
water.note: Water is present only in the cups. The card is the exchange of the element, not the element itself.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of water, not of fire.

vegetation.value: Absent (the wreaths are the only vegetation)
vegetation.note: The wreaths are the vegetation of the card. They mark the celebration.

stone.note: Stone is present as the distant house, the home the meeting points toward.

polarity.note: The Two of Cups' remedy-pair is the Two of Wands: water and fire, union and ambition. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Two of Cups' union is the Two of Wands' ambition: sometimes the partnership needs to be corrected by the willingness to make a decision.

prescribedAct.value: Meet someone today at their level, cup to cup, and let the meeting be equal.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of meeting. The Two of Cups' lesson is that the union is not the fusion; it is the equality.

detailedReading: The Two of Cups is the water element in its phase of union. Its numerical degree is two — the number of polarity and pairing — and the figures are two standing humans, facing each other, each holding a cup, with a caduceus between them and a winged lion's head above. The landscape is the open ground with a distant house. There is no written word, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human meeting, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the meeting. The prescribed act follows from this: meet someone today at their level, cup to cup, and let the meeting be equal. The remedy is ambition — the Two of Wands — because the union needs to be corrected by the willingness to make a decision.

name: Three of Cups
symbols: Three figures raise cups together — community, the shared toast.
Harvest food at their feet — abundance, gathered and shared.
Dancing posture — joy, the body's yes.
Varied dress — the group is made of distinct people, not a crowd.

reading.upright: The Three of Cups is shared joy: friendship, community, the pleasure of being together in abundance.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the community curdles: gossip, a third party interfering, or an excess that hides the isolation.

elementalRegister.value: Water (Cups; the raised cups, the shared table)
elementalRegister.note: The Three of Cups is the water element in its phase of celebration. The raised cups mark it as the card of friendship and community.

numericalDegree.note: Three is the number of creation and fruition. The card is the moment at which the pairing of the Two becomes a community.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Three is the first fruition of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: Three standing human figures, raising cups
figureType.note: The figures are human and grouped. Their number marks the card as one of community, not of the pair.

posture.note: The posture is one of celebration: the figures are open, moving, lifted.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of shared celebration. The cups are lifted as a group, not as individuals.

gaze.value: Looking at each other or at the cups
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the community. The figures are looking at each other and at the shared toast.

movementDirection.note: The movement is circular. The card is the dance of the community, not the procession of the individual.

centralObject.note: The cups are the central objects, the instruments of the shared toast.

heldObject.note: The cups are held, one in each hand. The holding is the holding of the shared offering.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human community, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the celebration: the cups that are raised.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The celebration is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A garden with harvest food at the feet
landscape.note: The landscape is the garden, the place of abundance. The harvest food marks the card as one of the gathered plenty.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The card is the open garden, not the household.

threshold.note: There is no threshold. The card is the celebration, not the crossing.

celestialBody.note: There is no celestial body. The celebration is ordinary, not cosmic.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The card is the warm day of the celebration.

symmetry.value: Balanced (the three figures around a shared point)
symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the community.

repetitionCount.note: The number three is the number of fruition. The three cups mark the card as one of community.

verticalAxis.value: The raised cups above the figures
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis is the axis of the toast: the cups are lifted above the figures.

horizontalAxis.value: The figures around a shared point
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the community: the figures are arranged around a shared center.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figures are upright and celebratory.

clothing.note: The varied dress marks the figures as distinct persons, not a uniform. The card is a community of distinct selves.

nudity.note: The figures are clothed. Their celebration is mediated by their social positions.

crown.note: There is no crown, but the wreaths are the mark of the celebration. The community is crowning itself with flowers.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of joy, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figures are free.

water.value: Absent (the cups are the only water)
water.note: Water is present only in the cups. The card is the shared drink, not the element itself.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of water, not of fire.

vegetation.note: The vegetation is the harvest, the mark of the abundance. It is the garden that has yielded its fruit.

stone.note: There is no stone. The card is a card of the garden, not of the castle.

polarity.note: The Three of Cups' remedy-pair is the Three of Wands: water and fire, celebration and expansion. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Three of Cups' celebration is the Three of Wands' expansion: sometimes the celebration needs to be corrected by the willingness to send the plan into the world.

prescribedAct.value: Celebrate one thing today with someone else, and let the shared joy be the point.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of shared joy. The Three of Cups' lesson is that the joy is not the same as the indulgence; it is the company.

detailedReading: The Three of Cups is the water element in its phase of celebration. Its numerical degree is three — the number of creation and fruition — and the figures are three standing humans, raising cups, with harvest food at their feet. The landscape is the garden, the place of abundance. There is no creature, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human community, not of instinct, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the community. The prescribed act follows from this: celebrate one thing today with someone else, and let the shared joy be the point. The remedy is expansion — the Three of Wands — because the celebration needs to be corrected by the willingness to send the plan into the world.

name: Four of Cups
symbols: A figure sits under a tree, arms crossed — withdrawal, and the refusal to be moved.
A fourth cup is offered from a cloud — the gift is missed by the downcast eyes.
Three cups sit at his feet — the abundance that is not being seen.
His gaze is fixed — the contemplation that has become a closed door.

reading.upright: The Four of Cups is apathy: withdrawal from what is available, contemplation that has become stuck, the offer that is not seen.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the Four of Cups opens: a new awareness arrives, the cup is finally taken up, and re-engagement begins.

elementalRegister.value: Water (Cups; the offered cup, the tree, the still figure)
elementalRegister.note: The Four of Cups is the water element in its phase of withdrawal. The still figure and the offered cup mark it as the card of apathy and the missed offer.

numericalDegree.note: Four is the number of structure and stability. The card is the moment at which the celebration of the Three hardens into withdrawal.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Four is the stabilization of the suit's energy, in its withdrawn form.

figureType.value: A seated human figure under a tree, arms crossed
figureType.note: The figure is human and closed. His crossed arms mark the card as one of refusal.

posture.value: Seated under a tree, arms crossed, head down
posture.note: The posture is one of withdrawal: the body is closed, the gaze is down, the figure is not open to the offer.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of refusal. The arms are crossed, marking the figure as closed to the offer.

gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of apathy. The figure is looking at the ground, not at the cup being offered.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the withdrawal.

centralObject.value: The fourth cup offered from the cloud
centralObject.note: The cup is the offer, missed by the downcast eyes. It is the central object of the card, the gift that is not seen.

heldObject.note: Nothing is held. The figure has not taken the offered cup.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human withdrawal, not of instinct.

tool.note: There is no tool. The card is the waiting, not the acting.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The withdrawal is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A tree, and three cups at the feet, with a fourth offered from a cloud
landscape.note: The landscape is the tree, the place of rest, and the three cups at the feet, the abundance that is not being seen.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The card is the open ground under the tree.

threshold.note: There is no threshold. The card is the stuck moment, not the crossing.

celestialBody.value: A cloud (the source of the offered cup)
celestialBody.note: The cloud is the celestial source of the offered cup. It marks the offer as one that comes from beyond the self.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The card is the calm day of the withdrawal.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the figure off-centre, the offered cup above)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The card is the withdrawal, not the balance.

repetitionCount.note: The number four is the number of structure. The four cups mark the card as one of the settled state of the withdrawal.

verticalAxis.value: The offered cup above, the figure below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis is the axis of the offer: the cup is offered from above, the figure is below, looking down.

horizontalAxis.value: The three cups at the feet
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the abundance: the three cups sit at the figure's feet, unseen.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figure is upright, though closed.

clothing.note: The simple robe marks the figure as one who has withdrawn from the world, not one who is engaged in it.

nudity.note: The figure is clothed. His withdrawal is mediated by his ordinary dress.

crown.note: There is no crown. The figure has no authority, and no triumph.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of apathy, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figure is free to take the cup.

water.value: Absent (the cups are the only water)
water.note: Water is present only in the cups. The card is the offer of the element, not the element itself.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of water, not of fire.

vegetation.note: The tree is the vegetation of the card. It marks the card as one of rest, not of growth.

stone.note: There is no stone. The card is a card of the ground, not of the castle.

polarity.note: The Four of Cups' remedy-pair is the Four of Wands: water and fire, apathy and celebration. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Four of Cups' apathy is the Four of Wands' celebration: sometimes the withdrawal needs to be corrected by the willingness to be celebrated.

prescribedAct.value: Look up once today, and take the offer that is being held out to you.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of openness. The Four of Cups' lesson is that the cup is already being offered; the missing is in the gaze.

detailedReading: The Four of Cups is the water element in its phase of withdrawal. Its numerical degree is four — the number of structure — and the figure is a seated man under a tree, arms crossed, with three cups at his feet and a fourth offered from a cloud. The landscape is the tree and the ground: the tree is the place of rest, the three cups at his feet are the abundance that is not being seen. There is no creature, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human withdrawal, not of instinct, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The asymmetry of the composition marks it as a card of the withdrawal, not the balance. The prescribed act follows from this: look up once today, and take the offer that is being held out to you. The remedy is celebration — the Four of Wands — because the apathy needs to be corrected by the willingness to be celebrated.

name: Five of Cups
symbols: A cloaked figure bows over three spilled cups — the grief is real, and it is being felt.
Two cups stand behind — what is still there, unacknowledged.
A river separates the figure from a bridge — the crossing that will come.
A dark cloak — the mourning, worn openly.

reading.upright: The Five of Cups is grief: the loss that must be felt, the regret that attends what has happened.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the Five of Cups begins to move: acceptance, the two remaining cups finally seen, the turning toward the bridge.

elementalRegister.value: Water (Cups; the spilled cups, the river, the cloak)
elementalRegister.note: The Five of Cups is the water element in its phase of grief. The spilled cups and the river mark it as the card of loss and mourning.

numericalDegree.note: Five is the number of the human figure and of disruption. The card is the moment at which the withdrawal of the Four breaks into the grief of the Five.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Five is the disruption of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: A cloaked standing human figure, bowed over the spilled cups
figureType.note: The figure is human and cloaked. His cloak marks him as one in mourning, and his bow marks the grief.

posture.note: The posture is one of grief: the body is bent, the head is down, the figure is not looking at what remains.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of mourning. The arms hang, marking the figure as one who has set down the burden of active life.

gaze.value: Downcast, fixed on the spilled cups
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of grief. The figure is looking at the loss, not at the two cups behind.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the grief.

centralObject.note: The spilled cups are the central objects, the loss that is being felt.

heldObject.note: Nothing is held. The figure's hands are empty, marking the card as one of loss.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human grief, not of instinct.

tool.note: There is no tool. The card is the grief, not the working through it.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The grief is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A river, a bridge, and a castle in the distance
landscape.note: The landscape is the river and the bridge: the river separates the figure from the bridge, and the bridge is the crossing that will come.

architecture.note: The bridge is the architecture of the crossing. It is distant, marking the card as the grief that is not yet passed.

threshold.note: The bridge is the threshold between the grief and the moving on. The figure has not yet crossed it.

celestialBody.note: There is no celestial body. The grief is ordinary, not cosmic.

weather.note: The weather is overcast. The card is the grey day of the grief.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the figure bowed to one side, the two cups behind)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The card is the grief, not the balance.

repetitionCount.note: The number five is the number of the human figure. The five cups mark the card as one of loss and what remains.

verticalAxis.value: The figure above the spilled cups
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis is the axis of the mourning: the figure stands above the spilled cups, bowed over them.

horizontalAxis.value: The two cups behind, the bridge in the distance
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of what remains: the two cups are behind, the bridge is in the distance.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figure is upright, though bowed.

clothing.note: The dark cloak is the mark of mourning. It marks the card as one of open grief.

nudity.note: The figure is clothed. His grief is mediated by his mourning dress.

crown.note: There is no crown. The figure is not a ruler; he is a mourner.

wound.note: There is no visible wound, but the loss is the injury. The card is the wound of grief.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figure is free to turn toward the two cups.

water.value: The river and the spilled cups
water.note: Water is present as the river and the spilled cups. The river is the crossing that will come; the spilled cups are the loss.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of water, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the bare ground, not of the garden.

stone.note: Stone is present as the bridge and the castle, the architecture of the crossing.

polarity.note: The Five of Cups' remedy-pair is the Five of Wands: water and fire, grief and conflict. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Five of Cups' grief is the Five of Wands' conflict: sometimes the grief needs to be corrected by the willingness to fight for what remains.

prescribedAct.value: Turn around once today, and see the two cups that are still standing behind you.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of turning. The Five of Cups' lesson is that the loss is real, but it is not the whole of what remains.

detailedReading: The Five of Cups is the water element in its phase of grief. Its numerical degree is five — the number of the human figure and of disruption — and the figure is a cloaked standing man, bowed over three spilled cups, with two cups standing behind and a river and bridge in the distance. The landscape is the river and the bridge: the river is the crossing that will come. There is no creature, no written word, and no binding: the card is a card of human grief, not of instinct, and not of restraint. The loss is the central mark of the card. The asymmetry of the composition marks it as a card of the grief, not the balance. The prescribed act follows from this: turn around once today, and see the two cups that are still standing behind you. The remedy is conflict — the Five of Wands — because the grief needs to be corrected by the willingness to fight for what remains.

name: Six of Cups
symbols: Two children in a courtyard — innocence, the childhood that is shared.
Six cups filled with white flowers — sweet memory, the gift of the past.
A figure walks away — leaving the courtyard, moving on.
Warm light on stone — the past, remembered kindly.

reading.upright: The Six of Cups is the sweetness of memory: nostalgia, reunion, the innocence that the past still offers.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the past has become a hiding place: an idealised memory that blocks the present, or the refusal to leave the courtyard.

elementalRegister.value: Water (Cups; the shared cups, the children)
elementalRegister.note: The Six of Cups is the water element in its phase of memory. The shared cups and the children mark it as the card of nostalgia and the sweet past.

numericalDegree.note: Six is the number of harmony and balance. The card is the moment at which the grief of the Five is resolved into the sweetness of the memory.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Six is the resolved memory of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: Two children in a courtyard, and a figure walking away
figureType.note: The children are the figures of innocence; the walking figure is the mark of the departure. The two together mark the card as one of memory and departure.

posture.value: The children standing or playing; the walking figure upright
posture.note: The posture is one of shared ease in the children, and of departure in the walking figure.

gesture.value: The children holding or sharing the cups
gesture.note: The gesture is one of shared offering. The cups are held as gifts, not as prizes.

gaze.value: The children looking at each other or at the cups; the walking figure looking away
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the shared memory in the children, and of the departure in the walking figure.

movementDirection.value: Static for the children; away for the walking figure
movementDirection.note: The movement is away. The card is the moment when the past is being left, but the memory remains.

centralObject.note: The cups are the central objects, the gifts of the memory. They are filled with flowers, the mark of the sweet past.

heldObject.note: The cups are held by the children. The holding is the holding of the memory.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human memory, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the memory: the cups that are shared.

name: Seven of Cups
symbols: A figure before seven floating cups — the array of options, none yet chosen.
Each cup holds something different — and some of what is shown cannot coexist.
A shadowy figure in the mist — the wish that is not what it seems.
One cup is crowned with a laurel — the one real prize among the phantoms.

reading.reversed: Reversed, the mist clears: a decisive choice, or the reality check that sorts the cup from the fantasy.

elementalRegister.note: The Seven of Cups is the water element in its phase of fantasy. The floating cups mark it as the card of choices and the imagination that offers more than it can deliver.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Seven is the testing of the suit's energy.

figureType.note: The figure is human and still. His stillness marks him as one faced with the choice, not one who has chosen.

posture.note: The posture is one of contemplation. The figure is facing the choices, not moving toward them.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of the choice not yet made. The arms are open to the field, not reaching for a single cup.

weather.note: The weather is misty. The card is the unclear day of the fantasy.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the cups are scattered, the figure to one side)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The card is the field of the choices, not a balance.

repetitionCount.note: The number seven is the number of the testing. The seven cups mark the card as one of the many options.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figure is free to choose.

water.note: Water is present as the mist and the cups. The mist is the unclear, the cups are the choices.

fire.value: A flame or a dragon in one cup

detailedReading: The Seven of Cups is the water element in its phase of fantasy. Its numerical degree is seven — the number of trial and testing — and the figure is a standing man facing seven floating cups, one laurel-crowned, one holding a dragon, one a shadowy figure. The remedy is defense — the Seven of Wands — because the fantasy needs to be corrected by the willingness to stand for one thing.

name: Eight of Cups
symbols: A figure walks away from eight stacked cups — the leaving is chosen, not forced.
A full moon above — the intuition that guides the departure.
A river and mountains ahead — the unknown the figure is walking toward.
The back is turned — the past is being deliberately left.

reading.upright: The Eight of Cups is the deliberate leaving: what has been built is set down, and the deeper thing is sought.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the leaving is refused: the fear that keeps one in place, or the return to what has already been left.

elementalRegister.value: Water (Cups; the stacked cups, the moon, the river)
elementalRegister.note: The Eight of Cups is the water element in its phase of departure. The stacked cups and the moon mark it as the card of the deliberate leaving.

numericalDegree.note: Eight is the number of regeneration and return. The card is the moment at which the field of the Seven is left behind and the departure begins.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Eight is the release of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: A cloaked standing human figure, walking away
figureType.note: The figure is human and cloaked. His cloak marks the card as one of departure, and his walking marks the leaving.

posture.value: Standing, walking away, back to the viewer
posture.note: The posture is one of departure: the back is turned, the figure is moving away from what was.

gesture.value: A staff in one hand, the other hand at the side
gesture.note: The gesture is one of support. The staff is the only tool the figure carries, marking the departure as one of bare necessity.

gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of departure. The figure is looking at the destination, not at the cups left behind.

movementDirection.note: The movement is away. The card is the deliberate leaving, not the return.

centralObject.note: The cups are the central objects, the thing that is being left. They are stacked, the mark of the accumulated past.

heldObject.note: The staff is the support of the walking figure. It is the only thing carried.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human departure, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tool is the staff, the support of the departure.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The departure is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A river, mountains, and a moon above

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The card is the open landscape, not the household.

threshold.note: The river is the threshold between the past and the future. The figure is crossing it.

celestialBody.note: The moon is the celestial body of the card. It is the guide of the departure, the light in the dark.

weather.note: The weather is clear and cool. The card is the night of the departure.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the figure walking away, the cups behind)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The card is the departure, not the balance.

repetitionCount.note: The number eight is the number of regeneration. The eight cups mark the card as one of the accumulated past.

verticalAxis.value: The moon above, the figure below

horizontalAxis.value: The figure walking away, the cups behind

clothing.note: The red cloak marks the figure as one of vitality, not of mourning. The departure is chosen, not forced.

crown.note: There is no crown. The figure is not a ruler; he is a walker.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of departure, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figure is free to leave.

water.note: Water is present as the river, the crossing that must be made. It is the boundary between the past and the future.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of water, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the bare landscape, not of the garden.

stone.note: Stone is present as the mountains, the destination that the figure is walking toward.

polarity.note: The Eight of Cups' remedy-pair is the Eight of Wands: water and fire, departure and speed. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Eight of Cups' slow departure is the Eight of Wands' speed: sometimes the leaving needs to be corrected by the swift motion.

prescribedAct.value: Leave one thing behind today that no longer serves you, and walk toward the moon.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of departure. The Eight of Cups' lesson is that the leaving is not the loss; it is the search for the deeper thing.

name: Nine of Cups
symbols: A figure sits, arms crossed, in a satisfied posture — the wish, granted.
Nine cups arc behind him — the fulfilment, gathered.
A red hat — the pleasure of the thing, worn openly.
A table cloth — the setting is at ease, not strained.

reading.reversed: Reversed, the satisfaction is hollow: a wish granted that does not satisfy, or a smugness that mistakes itself for happiness.

prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of recognition. The Nine of Cups' lesson is that the satisfaction is not the getting; it is the noticing.

name: Ten of Cups
symbols: A family group with arms raised — the household, together.
A rainbow of ten cups arches above — the blessing, complete.
A house in the background — the home that holds it.
A river flows through — life continues, and it is good.

reading.reversed: Reversed, the harmony is fractured: a broken home, a disconnection within the family, the ideal that has not been realised.

elementalRegister.note: The Ten of Cups is the water element in its phase of completion. The rainbow of cups marks it as the card of household harmony and belonging.

name: Page of Cups

A fish emerges from the cup — the unexpected message, the intuition surfacing.
A sea behind — the depth from which the message comes.

reading.reversed: Reversed, the sensitivity curdles: moodiness, emotional immaturity, or the retreat into an imagined world.

detailedReading: The Page of Cups is the youthful bearer of the water element, the card of sensitivity and wonder. Its elemental register is water, and its numerical degree is the Page, the student and messenger. The figure is a young human standing by the sea, holding a cup and looking into it, with a fish emerging from the cup and lotus flowers on the robe. The landscape is the sea, the depth from which the message comes. There is no architecture, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the Page is in the open, by the sea, free to receive.
